judge_verdict.summary: The agent shipped correct Python enum fast paths with large base speedups, but the verifier rightly failed because geometric-mean speedup versus the reference Rust commit (1.02) fell below the 1.1 pass threshold.

verdict.outcome_rationale: This is a fair agent-fault failure: the verifier recorded binary_reward 0 because the continuous gm_speedup_patch_commit score of 1.0208803820286128 did not clear the 1.1 pass gate [1][2][3]. The task asked to optimize the provided TypeAdapter enum-validation benchmark while preserving outputs and pursuing the best possible speedup [4], and the GSO harness grades that by comparing a pre-patch base, the agent patch (with per-test equivalence checks), and reference commit ac9e6ee that moves enum validation into Rust [5][6]. The agent made a substantive, on-target attempt—profiling showed time in Enum construction, it found no native enum support in pydantic-core 2.16.3, and it added value-map fast paths in pydantic/_internal/_std_types_schema.py plus a default-config TypeAdapter(Enum) bypass in pydantic/type_adapter.py [7][8]—and its own reruns reported roughly halving the instruction workload versus the ~0.10s baseline [8]. On the hidden suite all 20 post-patch runs passed equivalence [6], yet aggregate performance only matched the reference commit within about 2% (e.g., Test 7 patch times ~0.030s versus commit ~0.028–0.033s and base ~0.064–0.070s) [9], so it did not meet the task’s performance bar even though correctness held [3][9].

evidence.claim: The verifier’s binary pass gate requires continuous gm_speedup_patch_commit reward strictly above 1.1000.

citations.quote:
REWARD=$(cat /logs/verifier/reward.txt 2>/dev/null || echo "0")
THRESHOLD=1.1000
PASS=$(python3 -c "print(1 if float('$REWARD') > $THRESHOLD else 0)")
echo $PASS > /logs/verifier/reward.txt
